exercise1.hint: DictReader reads the header for you, so row["name"] and row["score"] work straight away. Typing the three lines out passes the first check and fails the second.

questions.prompt: Why use the csv module instead of splitting each line on commas?
choices: A quoted field can contain a comma, and split would break the row there
split does not work on files
questions.explain: "Lovelace, Ada" is one field with a comma in it. csv knows about the quotes; split sees three fields where there are two.

questions.prompt: What does csv.DictReader use the first line of the file for?
choices: As the column names for every row after it
As the first row of data
questions.explain: The header becomes the keys, which is why row["score"] works without you saying which position that is.

questions.prompt: What type is row["score"] straight out of a CSV file?
questions.explain: A file is text, so everything read out of one is text until you convert it. That is the source of more early bugs than anything else in this course.
